newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: NZ SPORT-Rixon considers couch therapy for batsmen.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-Rixon considers couch therapy for batsmen.

text.p: LAHORE, Nov 21 - New Zealand cricket coach Steve Rixon will consider enlisting specialist help to sort out the minds of his batsmen, NZPA reported on Friday (NZT).

After watching New Zealand surrender their first innings for 155 on the opening day of the first test against Pakistan, Rixon said a qualified psychologist could be called in to assist the team when they return to New Zealand next month.
"I'll have a close look at bringing in a specialist psychologist when we get home," Rixon said.
Christchurch sports psychologist Gilbert Enoka was called in to work with the national side during the latter stages of their disastrous 1994-95 centenary season in New Zealand.
The side's capitulation today was by no means the first time the batsmen have performed well below expectations on the tour of Sharjah and Pakistan.
Rixon has been working hard in one-on-one sessions with his frontline batsmen, trying to sort out their mental approaches and application.
"Psychologically, we need to do a bit of work with our batsmen," he said.
"It's a psychological thing, and it's going to take a lot more time than I first thought.
"When I first came to New Zealand I certainly had the impression that the (Stephen) Flemings and (Nathan) Astles and so forth were established. But they're basically only kids in the game.
"I've learnt a lot from the short time I've spent with them, but a lot more work has to go into getting them up psychologically.

"A good sign though is that when you're down you drop catches but both of those guys are still doing a good job with their hands. When you are really down and out every facet of your game is poor," Rixon said.
"I'd like to think that it will all be sorted out by the time we get home."
